neighbours.label: A non-initial word piece of a split Spanish or Portuguese (mostly Latin American) place name (Pat|agon|ia, Zam|ora, P|otos|í, G|rosso), not the same pieces in English words and not place names that are single tokens
fire: Many families from the capital spend weekends in Cuernavaca for the climate.
The tin miners of Cochabamba went on strike in the winter of 1947.
The bus to Ayacucho climbs through the Andes for almost ten hours.
Drug violence spread across Sinaloa in the early two thousands.
Oil was discovered beneath Lake Maracaibo in the 1910s.
The Roman bridge at Badajoz still carries foot traffic over the river.
The ranch lies in the dry hills outside Durango, north of the city.
Deforestation in Rondônia accelerated after the highway opened.
quiet: Many families from the capital spend weekends in Lima for the climate.
The tin miners of Bolivia went on strike in the winter of 1947.
The bus to the coast climbs through the Andes for almost ten hours.
Drug violence spread across Mexico in the early two thousands.
Oil was discovered beneath the lake in the 1910s.
The Roman bridge at Madrid still carries foot traffic over the river.
The ranch lies in the dry hills outside the city, near the dragon statue.
Deforestation in Chile accelerated after the highway opened.
